correctness.rationale: The proof identifies all primal extreme points as oriented graph-edge molecules, proves from first principles that dual extreme 1-Lipschitz potentials are exactly those with connected tight-edge subgraph, and then applies graph parity. Bipartiteness forces every dual extreme potential to saturate every edge; nonbipartiteness supplies a spanning-tree parity potential that is dual-extreme yet vanishes on some edge. McGregor's finite-dimensional iff criterion then yields exactly the stated equivalence. A pure-stdlib exhaustive checker corroborates the graph criterion for all 771 connected labeled graphs on 2 through 5 vertices and 16,716 dual extreme potentials. The enumeration is not used as proof of arbitrary order.

value.rationale: The claim gives a natural complete classification: a canonical graph property, bipartiteness, exactly determines whether the associated finite real Lipschitz-free space has the maximal numerical index. It simultaneously covers every finite tree and bipartite graph and excludes every graph with an odd cycle. The tight-edge connectivity lemma is a reusable structural description of the dual polytope, so the result is more than a routine family computation or parameter substitution.
